big: You are offered ₹1 lakh today or ₹1 lakh after three years. Take it today. Today's money can be put to work, so it is worth more than the same amount later.

lines: It is the same ₹1 lakh. Why does the date matter?
Because ₹1 lakh today can grow. At 10% a year it becomes ₹1.33 lakh in three years. So the later ₹1 lakh is worth less to you today.

note: Made-up figures, for learning only. FV = PV × (1+r)^n. PV = FV ÷ (1+r)^n.

alt: Bars of a growing sum over three years
caps: Each year adds interest on the amount so far.
After three years it is about ₹1.33 lakh.
Discounting is just this, run backwards.

q: ₹1,00,000 grows at 10% a year for 2 years. What is the future value?
why: ₹1,10,000 is the value after one year only.
₹2,00,000 would need a far higher rate.

q: ₹1,21,000 is due in 2 years and the rate is 10%. What is it worth today?
why: ₹1,21,000 ignores the time value of money.
₹79,000 subtracts 21% from the sum, which is wrong.

q: Why is ₹1 today worth more than ₹1 a year from now?
opts: The bank closes after a year
why: Money in hand can earn a return in the meantime.
Colour is not the reason. It does not fit the facts given.
Banks do not close for this reason. It does not answer what was asked.
Prices do change, and that does not explain this.

q: A friend says, 'This fund gives 12%.' What is missing?
opts: The fund's logo and its slogan
The name of the fund house
The period the rate applies to
why: A logo adds no information on the rate.
A name does not say what period 12% applies to.
A rate means little without the period it covers.
Colour is not data. That does not match this case.

pts: Always state the period with a rate.
